1. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., 1973 seeking quashing of FIR No. 132/2019 dated 11.03.2019 under Sections 406/498A/34 IPC, 1860 registered at Police Station Sagar Pur, Delhi,
and the subsequent proceedings arising therefrom on the grounds of settlement.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the parties submit that under the aegis of Delhi Mediation Centre at Patiala House Courts, New Delhi, the parties have been able to resolve their disputes and reduced the terms of settlement into writing vide report dated 04.09.2023.
3. According to the terms of settlement, both the parties after resolving their disputes had decided to give their marriage one more chance.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the parties have been residing together once again since the year 2019.

sentences.text:
After discussions in cordial atmosphere during the mediation proceedings the parties have settled all the above mentioned cases/disputes as under :-
(5.1) That the complainant/wife and respondent/husband.
Father-in-law Sh. Satish Kumar, Cousin Mother-in-law Smt. Nirmala Devi, Brother-in-law Sh. Pankaj Kumar and Nikhil Kumar have amicably settled their disputes without any pressure, force or coercion.
(5.2) All the parties/family members agreed to forget and keep aside all their disputes and grievances occurred prior to this settlement and shall maintain healthy, cordial relation with each other.

(5.3) It is agreed between the parties that all pending cases against each other after this settlement shall withdrawn and quashed with concerned court in following manner:-
i.

Sh. Satish Kumar shall withdraw and close his case CS/SCJ/1067/2018 pending before the Hon 'ble Court of Senior Civil Judge, Patiala House Court, New Delhi once for all against Ms. Nidhi and Sh. Sonu Kumar within 30 days of this settlement.

7. This Court has interacted with respondent no.2 who affirms her statement made in the affidavit and submits that she is happy in her marriage now.
She further submits that she has no further disputes pending with the petitioner and she is happily cohabiting with the petitioner alongwith their son since 2019.
She affirms that she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed.
8. The parties shall remain bound by the terms of settlement as also the statement made before this Court today.

9. In view of the fact that the parties have amicably reconciled their differences and are cohabiting,
this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served in continuing with the aforesaid FIR and the proceeding emanating therefrom.

Moreover, since the disputes have been resolved and the parties have come together, the pendency of the FIR and the proceedings emanating therefrom would not be conducive for their cohabitation and would disrupt their matrimonial life.
10. Accordingly, FIR No. 132/2019 dated 11.03.2019 under Sections 406/498A/34 IPC, 1860 registered at Police Station Sagar Pur, Delhi, and the subsequent proceedings arising therefrom are quashed.
11. The petition stand disposed of.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J OCTOBER 19, 2023 Aj
